entities.summary: Riccardo Petroni was a senior cardinal in the Roman Catholic Church during the closing decades of the thirteenth century and the early years of the fourteenth century. Born into a prominent family in Siena, Italy, Petroni rose through the ranks of the Church, becoming a key advisor to Pope John XXII. He played a pivotal role in the Papal Schism, a period of conflict between the Avignon Papacy and the Roman Papacy, which had far-reaching consequences for the Catholic Church and European politics. Petroni's influence extended beyond the Church, as he was a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Black Death relief efforts in Italy. His legacy can be seen in the continued development of the Catholic Church's hierarchical structure and the rise of the Conciliar movement, which aimed to reform the Church from within. Despite his significant impact, Petroni's life remains somewhat of a mystery, with many details lost to the sands of time. Nevertheless, his contributions to the Church's history and European politics make him a figure worthy of recognition.
